title: Incremental Shedding and Graceful Model Continuity
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an operational approach for staged, minimally invasive capacity shedding coupled with model-semantics-aware downgrades across regions. The goal is to keep client-facing latency and error surfaces predictable while preserving correctness for high-SLO workloads. This is a working doc for platform engineers; it intentionally mixes architecture patterns with checklists and incident runbook fragments.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to request routing/control plane decisions in Redwood Hosted and Dedicated clusters, and the Private control plane when configured for multi-region failover.
- Customers can pin model families and SLO classes (e.g., gold/silver/bronze).
- Models are grouped into families by semantic equivalence (exact-replica, quantized, distilled, small-family).
- Network partitions and regional GPU exhaustion are primary triggers for this play.

Key goals:
1) Avoid hard global outages: prefer scaled-down continuity over abrupt rejects.
2) Preserve correctness for high-priority customers and critical routes.
3) Ensure predictable cost profile during stress (avoid expensive autoscaling spikes).
4) Provide clear, testable policy semantics so downstream teams can reason about behavior.

High-level pattern summary:
- Admission control is layered: global throttles -> region budgets -> tenant quotas -> route-level limits -> model-family substitution.
- Degradation is incremental: scaling back batch sizes and async features first, then model downgrades, then regional spillover, then tail-trimming (late token termination), then rejects.
- Control plane uses a scored decision graph (priority score + cost delta + semantic distance) to choose among options. Decisions are deterministic given the same inputs to aid reproducibility.

Control plane decision flow (conceptual):
1) Detect stress: sustained 95th-latency > configured SLO factor or GPU utilization > 90% for X minutes.
2) Compute candidate mitigations (list ordered by severity): reduce batch target, enable prefix KV-cache, route to secondary region, switch model from family A->A-quant, degrade context length, soft-throttle low-priority tenants.
3) Score candidates by: impact_on_SLO (higher is worse), semantic_distance (higher is worse), cost_delta (positive if more cost), and rollback_complexity.
4) Apply lowest-severity, lowest-risk action with breach delta > threshold. Re-evaluate every control window (30s).

Admission control and shedding tiers (operational definitions):
- Tier 0 (No degradation): normal operation.
- Tier 1 (Non-invasive): prefer queue shaping and batch sizing, cache warmups. Visible only in metrics, not API-level changelog.
- Tier 2 (Service-level degrade): reduce max context, disable streaming chunking, switch to quantized model variants with semantic_distance <= 0.2 (see mapping table). Returns 200 but notes degrade in audit headers.
- Tier 3 (Regional spill and tenant shedding): preemptible capacity engaged; best-effort for bronze tenants (probabilistic admission), silver tenants get degraded models, gold tenants preserved.
- Tier 4 (Aggressive): route to most-compact model family, trim long completions, start 429s for low-priority routes.

Model-variant mapping and semantic guidance:
- Families and canonical mapping (example):
  * family-bert-3B: canonical -> bert-3B-fp16, fallback -> bert-3B-4bit (quant), alt -> bert-distilled-1.2B (distilled)
  * family-gptx-13B: canonical -> gptx-13B-fp16, fallback -> gptx-13B-8bit, alt -> gptx-6B-distilled
- Semantic distance: a unitless score (0.0 = identical, 1.0 = orthogonal) computed by offline evals on representative prompt-suite. Use thresholds: <=0.15 for safe auto-swap, 0.15-0.35 require customer opt-in or downgrade headers, >0.35 avoid unless extreme.
- Quantized variants can be auto-enabled if latency improvement > 20% and semantic_distance <= 0.18.

Regional spillover mechanics (safe spill rules):
- Preferred region selection order is: local-affinity zone -> customer-preferred region -> nearby region (latency penalty <= 40ms) -> distant region (latency penalty > 40ms).
- Spillover policy must respect data residency tags. If a tenant has residency constraints, routing to alternate regions is blocked; instead, apply model downgrades and quota throttles.
- Circuit-breaker: if cross-region RTT degradation increases tail latency for > 3 consecutive control windows, roll back cross-region spill for affected tenant classes.
- Warm-standby lanes: maintain a small fraction of capacity in each region for incoming spill traffic (target 3%–7% of peak for 99th percentile protection).

Probabilistic holdback and canary softening:
- When enabling a new reduced-cost path (e.g., quant variant), do a probabilistic holdback: 10% of requests continue to canonical model for N minutes and compare perplexity/quality metrics. If drift < configured delta, increase to 50% then 100%.
- Maintain per-tenant and per-route feature flags so opt-in customers can accept more-aggressive degradation for cost-savings.

Observability, KPIs and alarms (must be present):
- Control metrics: decisions_per_minute, actions_applied_by_tier, rollback_count.
- Capacity metrics: gpu_util_1m/5m/15m, queued_requests, backpressure_events.
- Quality metrics: semantic_drift_pct (per model swap), eval_mismatch_rate (example prompts), user-reported-regressions.
- Customer impact: per-tenant error_rate, latency_p50/p95/p99, routing_region (for spillovers).
- Alarms: 1) sustained p95 latency > SLO*1.3 for 3 windows -> auto-tier1. 2) semantic_drift_pct > 2% after model swap -> immediate rollback. 3) cross-region-error-rate > 1% -> disable cross-region routing.

Simulation scenarios (recommended tests):
1) Sudden load spike in single region: simulate +200% qps; verify tier1 and tier2 actions before any 429s; check that gold tenants maintained within SLO.
2) Gradual GPU degradation: force a group of nodes to slow; ensure probabilistic holdback for quant swaps and that rollback works when drift observed.
3) Regional outage: blackhole region, verify warm-standby absorbs up to the target %, beyond that bronze tenants shed first and silver reduced to quantized variants.
4) Data residency conflict: mark tenant-residency and simulate spill; ensure no cross-region routing and that local model downgrades are used instead.

Operational runbook (incident snippets):
- Trigger: control-plane flags tier2 for region us-west-2 due to sustained 95th latency overshoot.
Steps:
  1) Confirm metrics: check gpu_util, queued_requests, decisions_applied in last 10 minutes.
  2) Review applied actions in audit log (control-plane/decisions). If only batch-size and cache applied, watch 3 windows.
  3) If model swaps executed and semantic_drift_pct > threshold -> initiate rollback: set control-plane override to force canonical models for gold customers, keep quant for bronze.
  4) If cross-region spill active and increasing p99 > SLO*1.5 -> disable cross-region spill for tenant classes except gold.
  5) Communicate: post incident note to #platform-ops with short summary and action-id.

Pre-deploy checklist (policy changes or new variant):
- Bench: perf delta (latency, throughput) for canonical vs candidate variant at representative seq-lens.
- Eval: semantic distance against benchmark prompt-suite (share report id).
- Rollout plan: probabilistic holdback percentages and monitoring dashboards.
- Feature flags: ensure per-tenant opt-out and global kill-switch available.
- Playbook update: add any new tier mapping to this doc and update Confluence link in linked_artifacts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Formalize how to compute semantic_distance automatically from lightweight online A/B signals.
- Explore cost-signal integration: allow rules that prefer cheaper options during budget-window for cost-conscious tenants.
- Define exact numeric thresholds for bronze/silver/gold in product billing docs and encode into control plane.

Appendix: quick policy examples (pseudo expressions)
- Soft-throttle rule: when gpu_util > 0.9 and tenant_priority == bronze then admission_rate = max(0.2, 1 - (gpu_util - 0.9)*5)
- Model-swap guard: allow_swap = (semantic_distance <= 0.18) AND (latency_improvement >= 0.2)
- Cross-region eligibility: eligible = (region_latency_penalty <= 40ms) AND (tenant_residency == false)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally prioritizes deterministic, auditable decision-making over opaque ML-based controllers. Once stable, we should prototype an RL-style optimizer but keep deterministic fallback as the source-of-truth.
- Please add comments inline with tags: [ops], [policy], [data-residency].

End of doc.
